extracted.intended_audience: aspiring and early-career historical fiction writers (and authors seeking genre-specific editing)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for crafting historically grounded fiction that balances research-driven authenticity with compelling narrative, plus the editor's role in refining accuracy, character, and structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose your era wisely
rubrics_metrics.description: Select a time period that not only interests you but also has enough historical information available to support your story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pick an era you are passionate about (examples given: Renaissance Italy, American Civil War, 19th‑century London); passion will fuel the hours of research required. Favor eras with sufficient primary and secondary sources to avoid speculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dive deep into research
rubrics_metrics.description: Research is the cornerstone of historical fiction—immerse yourself in the period beyond dates and events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand social customs, language, fashion, economic conditions, and daily life. Use primary sources (letters, diaries, newspapers) plus historical texts, academic papers, and other historical novels for context and depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop authentic characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters should be a product of their time, yet relatable to modern readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may use historical figures or fictional characters; fictional characters give freedom to explore nuances. Ensure beliefs, decisions, and conflicts are true to the period while resonating with contemporary themes like love, loss, ambition, and resilience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a compelling plot that weaves in historical elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Intertwine fictional narrative with historical events and settings so the plot and characters remain central.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance historical backdrop with character journeys; the historical material should enrich the story rather than overshadow it. Integrate events and settings in ways that advance character development and narrative stakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay attention to detail, but don't get lost in it
rubrics_metrics.description: Use historical details to enhance setting and mood, but avoid letting minutiae detract from narrative flow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize narrative clarity and character development over strict adherence to every historical fact. Excessive detail can bog down pacing—choose details that serve story and immersion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek feedback and be open to revision
rubrics_metrics.description: After drafting, obtain critiques—especially from readers knowledgeable about the era—and revise accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beta readers can identify inaccuracies, anachronisms, and opportunities to deepen historical context. Be prepared to revise to improve historical fidelity and storytelling balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Never stop learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat writing historical fiction as an ongoing learning process that continues after publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continue researching and refining your craft; each story offers opportunities to discover new aspects of the periods you write about.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance authenticity with storytelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a nuanced equilibrium between historical precision and the vibrancy of narrative fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive to make the past tangible and relatable without turning the manuscript into a history lesson. The tension between fact and fiction is central—use it to strengthen emotional truth and reader engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensuring historical accuracy (editor role)
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify dates, events, settings, language, and customs to prevent inaccuracies and anachronisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors act as fact-checkers who catch errors that may elude the writer. This includes checking for anachronistic details and confirming the plausibility of social behaviors and material culture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balancing fact with fiction (editor guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Help the writer weave historical facts seamlessly into the narrative so the story flows without excessive exposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors suggest ways to integrate historical events or figures to enrich the plot without compromising readability or historical integrity. They advise where to simplify or compress facts for narrative clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character development (editor role)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advise on creating complex, era-appropriate characters who remain relatable to modern readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors provide insights on motivations, social constraints, and how to render dialogue that reflects period speech patterns without alienating contemporary audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhancing narrative structure (editor role)
rubrics_metrics.description: Refine the manuscript's structure to maintain pace and ensure historical events are integrated smoothly into character arcs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors identify where the story lags or becomes confusing, recommending structural revisions, pacing changes, or reordering of events to improve clarity and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Providing genre-specific feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer market-aware, genre-specific critique based on knowledge of reader expectations and trends in historical fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors can help position a book in a crowded market by highlighting elements that make the work resonate with target readers and suggesting adjustments to meet genre conventions or innovate within them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouraging authenticity and sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure portrayal of people, cultures, and sensitive topics is respectful, accurate, and contextually appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors guide authors on representing marginalized groups, handling controversies, and avoiding harmful stereotypes or simplistic portrayals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crafting a cohesive manuscript (traditional editing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform standard editorial tasks—improving grammar, punctuation, syntax, coherence, and consistent style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond historical and structural concerns, editors ensure the manuscript reads smoothly, the author's voice is consistent, and technical issues are resolved prior to submission or publication.
